content.title: What are Map, HashMap & TreeMap?
content.description: Map is an interface used to store data as key-value pairs. HashMap is a hash table implementation that provides fast access, while TreeMap stores entries in sorted order based on keys.

content.content: Unlike collections such as List and Set, a Map stores data as key-value pairs. Every key must be unique, while values may be duplicated. The most commonly used implementations are HashMap for fast lookups and TreeMap for maintaining sorted keys.

content.title: Why Learn Maps?
content.content: Maps are widely used for fast searching, caching, configuration management, databases, and storing relationships between keys and values.
A Map associates every unique key with a value. Duplicate keys are not allowed, but duplicate values are permitted.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Maps are optimized for retrieving values using unique keys rather than indexes.

content.content: HashMap stores entries using a hash table. It provides fast insertion, deletion, and searching, but it does not guarantee any ordering of keys.

content.title: HashMap Example
Important Note
content.content: HashMap allows one null key and multiple null values.
TreeMap stores entries in sorted order of keys using a Red-Black Tree. It is useful when ordered data is required.

content.title: TreeMap Example
Sorting Feature
content.content: TreeMap automatically sorts entries according to the natural ordering of keys or a custom Comparator.

content.title: Traversing a Map
Map Performance
content.time_complexity: HashMap: O(1) Average, TreeMap: O(log n)

items.question: Student Records
items.answer: Store roll numbers as keys and student names as values.

items.question: Caching
items.answer: Retrieve data quickly using unique keys.

items.question: Configuration Settings
items.answer: Store property names and corresponding values.

content.title: Phone Contacts
content.content: A Map is like your phone contacts. Each phone number (key) uniquely identifies a contact (value). You search using the number or name key to find the corresponding information.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about HashMap internals, hashing, collision handling, TreeMap sorting, null keys, equals(), hashCode(), and differences between HashMap, LinkedHashMap, and TreeMap.

items.question: Can duplicate keys exist in a Map?
items.answer: No. Inserting the same key replaces the existing value.

items.question: Does HashMap maintain insertion order?
items.answer: No. Use LinkedHashMap when insertion order is required.

items.question: Can TreeMap store null keys?
items.answer: No. TreeMap throws a NullPointerException for null keys.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use HashMap for fast lookups and TreeMap when sorted keys are required.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: HashMap provides fast access using hashing.
Use put() to insert and get() to retrieve values.
entrySet() is commonly used for traversing maps.
